paper_style.palette_strategy: Booktabs tables use black/gray. Direct evaluation and train-before-test are consistently blue/orange (approximately #0173B2/#DE8F05); heatmaps use the source-exact Seaborn YlGnBu_r sequential palette with a 0–1 colorbar; PCA bars reuse one color; Figure 1 cycles husl colors by model and Figures 7/11 use family categorical colors. Numeric annotations provide partial redundancy for heatmaps and bars, but the 61-color rank plot is not grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Most bars, lines, text, axes and table rules are PDF vector objects. Heatmap cells/colorbars and some imported plot surfaces include rasterized/indexed resources; the resulting figures are mixed vector/raster, while Tables 1–8 are predominantly vector text/rules.
paper_style.style_consistency: The ICLR two-column main paper uses stable serif body/caption typography and sans-serif plot text, booktabs tables, repeated direct/TBT paired panels, and shared 0–1 Kendall/PCA axes. Appendix matrices preserve task order and color domains. Main weaknesses are the missing legends for Figure 11 and the 61-series Figure 1, plus short captions for several tables and appendix plots.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Rankings of 61 language models on two question-answering benchmarks: Natural Questions Open and ARC Challenge. Top: Direct evaluation leads to inconsistent rankings. Although both benchmarks test for question-answering ability, the resulting model rankings show substantial disagreement. Bottom: Train-before-test aligns model rankings. Note: For each of the two plots, we greedily align model rankings as much as possible without violating confidence intervals, thus revealing only those ranking changes that are statistically significant. See Appendix C.1.

color.semantic_mapping: Each color identifies one model and is reused in both direct and train-before-test panels; translucent bands encode rank intervals.

encodings.x: The two benchmark endpoints, Natural Questions Open and ARC Challenge
encodings.y: Model rank, reversed so rank 1 is at the top
encodings.color: Model identity across the two panels
encodings.line: A connecting rank path for each model
encodings.facet: Two vertical panels: Direct evaluation and Train-before-test
encodings.text: Model labels at the left, endpoint rank numbers at the right, and panel titles

figures.data_and_statistics: 61 models are ranked on each of two QA benchmarks. Rank intervals are derived from score confidence intervals; Appendix C.1's Algorithms 1–3 constrain the greedy alignment so only statistically significant changes are exposed. Direct rankings cross densely, whereas TBT rankings are visually more aligned. No error bars or seed aggregation are shown beyond the rank bands.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction's contradictory-ranking problem leads to equal benchmark-specific preparation; this local two-task demonstration is then generalized by Figures 2–5 and supported by the C.1 ranking algorithms.
design_strengths: A single view makes rank reversals and the shared model identity concrete.
The same color mapping across panels and the reversed rank axis make directional movement legible.
The confidence-rank band preserves the paper's significance-aware qualification.
design_weaknesses: Sixty-one colored paths are crowded and have no 61-item legend.
Color is not redundant with shape or line style and is weak in grayscale.
The exact interval and greedy-ordering semantics require Appendix C.1.
figures.reusable_pattern: For two rankings of the same entities, use paired bump panels with a shared identity color, reversed rank axis, endpoint labels, and an uncertainty band; above roughly twenty entities, add filtering or a searchable legend.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Mean ranking agreement between each benchmark and all others. We calculate Kendall’s τ between each benchmark and every other benchmark, and then average the results. Compared to direct evaluation, train-before-test consistently improves ranking agreement. A detailed comparison of Kendall’s τ values for every benchmark pair is provided in Appendix B.1. On average, the overall average Kendall’s τ is 0.52 for direct evaluation and 0.76 for train-before-test.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue denotes Direct evaluation and orange denotes Train-before-test.

encodings.x: 24 benchmark names, sorted by their direct-evaluation mean
encodings.color: Evaluation scheme: Direct evaluation versus Train-before-test
encodings.text: Rotated benchmark tick labels and y-axis tick labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Each bar is the mean Kendall τ between one benchmark and the other 23 benchmarks. Across all 276 pairs, the aggregate mean is 0.52 for direct evaluation and 0.76 for TBT; bars are point estimates without intervals or pair counts.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 1's local rank contrast becomes the paper's headline over 24 tasks; Figures 9–10 preserve the pairwise matrix behind these per-benchmark averages.
design_strengths: The paired bars and common 0–1 scale make the direction of improvement immediate.
Sorting by the direct baseline preserves the baseline difficulty gradient.
The caption supplies the aggregation denominator and points to the complete matrices.
design_weaknesses: Twenty-four rotated labels are dense.
Averaging hides pairwise heterogeneity and provides no uncertainty display.
The direct/TBT colors require the small legend and are not sufficient in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed task order and a common 0–1 axis for per-task baseline/method bars, then link to a full pairwise matrix for auditability.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Cross-category ranking agreement for direct evaluation (left) and train-before-test (right). We categorize benchmarks into language understanding (LU), commonsense reasoning (CR), question answering (QA), physics/biology/chemistry (PBC), math (Math), and medicine (Med), see Table 1. Kendall’s τ is averaged across all pairs of benchmarks that belong to two given categories. The diagonal entries represent intra-category agreement and the others represent inter-category agreement. Train-before-test improves both intra- and inter-category ranking agreement in all instances.

color.semantic_mapping: YlGnBu_r intensity encodes mean Kendall τ from 0 to 1; cell text provides the rounded value.

encodings.x: Six benchmark categories: LU, CR, QA, PBC, Math, Med
encodings.color: Mean Kendall τ for pairs of benchmarks across the category pair
encodings.text: Two-decimal cell annotations and category tick labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Each cell averages Kendall τ over benchmark pairs in two categories; the diagonal uses intra-category pairs and off-diagonals use inter-category pairs. Reported examples include LU 0.52→0.75 and Math 0.55→0.84; all shown instances improve.
figures.evidence_relation: The overall mean in Figure 2 is decomposed into category-level intra/inter evidence; Figure 13 repeats the same geometry for ties-aware τ-b.
design_strengths: Identical panel geometry and color domain support left/right comparison.
Diagonal semantics are stated, preventing an intra/inter mix-up.
Numeric annotations retain the value when color contrast is imperfect.
design_weaknesses: Heatmap color and small text compete at PDF scale.
Category means hide pair counts and within-category outliers.
Color is the main quantitative encoding despite the numerical labels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use paired category heatmaps with a fixed order, identical sequential scales, diagonal/off-diagonal definitions, and values printed in cells; add pair counts when category sizes differ.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Ranking agreement between perplexity rankings and downstream benchmark rankings under direct evaluation (top) and train-before-test (bottom). Perplexity rankings are consistent with each other under both evaluation schemes, with an average Kendall’s τ of 0.76 and 0.78, respectively. However, for direct evaluation, agreement between perplexity rankings and downstream rankings is low, with an average Kendall’s τ of just 0.48. Fortunately, train-before-test results in higher agreement between perplexity and downstream, increasing average Kendall’s τ to 0.74.

color.semantic_mapping: YlGnBu_r intensity encodes Kendall τ; cell text gives the corpus/benchmark value.

encodings.color: Kendall τ between corpus perplexity ranking and downstream ranking
encodings.text: Cell values, corpus labels, panel titles, and colorbar labels

figures.data_and_statistics: The matrix cells are Kendall τ between each of three 2025 perplexity corpora and each downstream benchmark, under each evaluation scheme. Perplexity-to-perplexity mean τ is 0.76/0.78, while perplexity-to-downstream increases from 0.48 to 0.74; no cell uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: The Figure 2 ranking-agreement claim is probed for a measurement connection: Figure 4 compares perplexity and downstream under the same regime, while Figure 5 changes the model training state.
design_strengths: Rows expose cross-corpus consistency rather than only one pooled score.
Top/bottom panels keep task columns aligned.
The colorbar and annotations make a dense cross-metric lookup possible.
design_weaknesses: Twenty-four columns and two colorbars leave little reading space.
Caption does not give row document counts or the Gemma exclusion context.
Point estimates lack corpus/task uncertainty.
figures.reusable_pattern: Represent measurement-source-by-task agreement as a rows-by-tasks heatmap with paired evaluation panels; state row sample sizes and exclusions alongside it.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: Ranking agreement between perplexity rankings before fine-tuning (direct evaluation) and downstream benchmark rankings after fine-tuning (train-before-test) for base models (top) and instruction-tuned models (bottom). Unlike Figure 4 where both rankings in each comparison use the same evaluation scheme, here we test whether pre-fine-tuning perplexity can predict post-fine-tuning downstream performance. Base models show strong correlation (average Kendall’s τ = 0.78), suggesting perplexity is a good predictor of model potential. This indicates that the ranking consistency we observe reflects inherent model potential rather than artifacts introduced by fine-tuning. Instruction-tuned models show much weaker correlation (average Kendall’s τ = 0.51).

color.semantic_mapping: YlGnBu_r intensity encodes Kendall τ; cell text supplies rounded values.

encodings.color: Agreement between direct pre-FT perplexity and TBT post-FT downstream rankings

figures.data_and_statistics: Each cell compares direct pre-fine-tuning perplexity ranking with TBT post-fine-tuning downstream ranking. Average τ is 0.78 for base models and 0.51 for instruction-tuned models; this is a cross-state point-estimate comparison with no intervals.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 4's same-regime perplexity connection is tested across pre/post fine-tuning states; the IT result is an explicit boundary on the latent-potential interpretation.
design_strengths: The same heatmap grammar as Figure 4 isolates the model-state change.
The caption makes the pre/post and direct/TBT roles explicit.
Base and IT heterogeneity is visible rather than collapsed into one claim.
design_weaknesses: The two 3×24 matrices remain difficult to read at page scale.
Model counts and Gemma exclusions are not in the figure.
No uncertainty or significance key accompanies the 0.78/0.51 cells.
figures.reusable_pattern: Separate same-state and cross-state ranking questions into matched heatmaps; put training state in panel titles and in the caption, not only in surrounding prose.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: Explained variance ratios of the top five principal components of the benchmark score matrix, under direct evaluation (left) and train-before-test (right). Train-before-test substantially increases the amount of variance explained by the first principal component, from 70% to 86%. This indicates the model potential is dominated by one single latent factor.

color.semantic_mapping: One blue bar series per panel; panel title encodes direct versus TBT.

encodings.text: Percentage labels above bars and panel titles

figures.data_and_statistics: PCA is applied to the standardized 24-benchmark score matrix; the first five components explain about 91% (direct) and 97% (TBT), with PC1 changing from 70% to 86%. Bars and percentage annotations are point estimates.
figures.evidence_relation: Category-level agreement in Figure 3 is followed by a score-matrix structural diagnostic; Figures 7–8 and Table 8 test the PC1 interpretation against compute and family slices.
design_strengths: Same 0–1 y-axis and five-component order make concentration visible.
Percentage labels make the PC1 contrast legible without estimating bar height.
The paired layout avoids confusing overall variance with a family-specific case.
design_weaknesses: Rounded percentages hide small residual component differences.
PCA preprocessing and sign convention are not encoded in the panel.
The latent-factor interpretation goes beyond what bars alone identify.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use paired explained-variance bars with identical component order and direct annotations when communicating a low-dimensionality transition; state standardization and cumulative sums in caption/prose.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: PC1 scores under train-before-test align with the pre-training compute.

color.semantic_mapping: Point color identifies Pythia, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, or Yi family.

encodings.text: Axis labels, ticks, and family legend

Family colors expose within- and between-family structure.
The paired Table 4 makes each plotted cost derivation auditable.

No trend line or numeric association is reported.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Explained variance ratios of the top five principal components of the QWEN score matrix. For train-before-test, the explained variance ratio of PC1 increases to 93%. Controlling the model family to QWEN has made the score matrix essentially rank one.

color.semantic_mapping: One blue bar series per direct/TBT panel; panel title carries the condition.

figures.data_and_statistics: PCA is recomputed on the Qwen-only score matrix. PC1 increases from 74% under direct evaluation to 93% under TBT; the remaining four components are shown as rounded percentages, without uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: This family-controlled case follows Figure 6's all-model PCA and is cross-checkable against the Qwen row in Table 8; it narrows rather than proves the rank-one interpretation.
design_strengths: Identical component order and y-axis make the Qwen change comparable with Figure 6.
PC1 percentage is directly annotated.
The family-control boundary is visible in both title and caption.
design_weaknesses: A single family cannot establish a general family-invariant mechanism.
No Qwen sample count or preprocessing detail is in the caption.
Rounded bars do not convey stability or uncertainty.
figures.reusable_pattern: Repeat the aggregate PCA visual on a controlled family slice with the same axes and labels, then provide all families in a companion table.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Figure 10: Cross benchmark ranking agreement under train-before-test. Benchmarks are sorted based on the training dataset size. Kendall’s τ is calculated for every benchmark pair.

caption.text: Figure 11: PC1 scores under train-before-test.

color.semantic_mapping: Bar color is intended to identify model family, but the figure provides no family legend.

figures.label: Figure 12

caption.text: Figure 12: Mean ranking agreement between each benchmark and all others, measured by Kendall’s tau-b, with non-statistically significant performance differences being treated as ties. We calculate Kendall’s τ-b between each benchmark and every other one, and then average. Compared to direct evaluation, train-before-test consistently improves ranking agreement–often by a large margin. On average, the overall average Kendall’s τ is 0.58 for direct evaluation and 0.77 for train-before-test.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/orange encode direct/TBT, while tau-b and ties are a statistical treatment rather than a color encoding.

encodings.x: 24 benchmark names in the Figure 2 order
encodings.text: Rotated benchmark labels and y ticks

figures.data_and_statistics: Each bar averages ties-aware Kendall tau-b between a benchmark and the other benchmarks. Overall mean tau-b is 0.58 for direct and 0.77 for TBT; non-significant model comparisons are treated as ties and no interval is drawn.
figures.evidence_relation: This is the significance-aware robustness re-expression of Figure 2; Figures 13–15 carry the same treatment to category and full pair matrices.
design_strengths: It changes the estimand while preserving the main Figure 2 geometry.
The caption defines ties and reports the aggregate result.
The same method colors make the robustness comparison visually cheap to parse.
design_weaknesses: The caption's phrase 'large margin' is not accompanied by a margin/error encoding.
Task labels remain dense and pair-level tie counts are absent.
The figure does not show how many comparisons become ties.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a statistical robustness analysis, retain the original bar ordering, colors, and axis domain while stating the alternate estimand and tie rule in the caption.

Kendall’s τ-b is averaged across all pairs of benchmarks that belong to two given categories. The diagonal represents the intra-category agreement and the others represent the inter-category agreement. train-before-test improves both intra- and inter-category ranking agreement in all instances.

The caption defines ties and diagonal semantics.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: We categorize benchmarks into language understanding (LU), commonsense reasoning (CR), question answering (QA), physics/biology/chemistry (PBC), math (Math), and medicine (Med).

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; this is a taxonomy table, not a performance estimate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six category rows list all 24 benchmark names; benchmark counts are implicit in the comma-separated cells.
tables.evidence_relation: Defines the category axes used in Figures 3/13 and the grouping logic behind the full matrices in Figures 9/10/14/15.
design_strengths: Compact two-column key fixes the task taxonomy.
Black-and-white booktabs is robust to printing.
The category abbreviations recur consistently in heatmaps.
design_weaknesses: Long benchmark lists are dense in the second column.
The caption does not state per-category counts or evaluation metrics.
The right-column float requires readers to connect it to later figures.
tables.reusable_pattern: Declare the benchmark taxonomy once in a compact two-column table and reuse the exact category order in every matrix.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Models considered, categorized by model family.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; this table enumerates model membership.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six family rows enumerate 61 model suffixes, including base and instruction-tuned variants; no performance values are present.
tables.evidence_relation: Supplies the model denominator for all results, the family mapping for Figure 7/11 and Tables 4/7/8, and the population behind Figure 1.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Bits per byte (BPB) of eight excluded GEMMA models compared to PYTHIA-410M across the three newly collected corpora. The GEMMA models exhibit abnormally high BPB values on Wiki and Stack, likely due to the greater average sequence length in these two datasets. Specifically, Arxiv has an average of 163 words per document, compared to 250 for Stack and 1502 for Wiki.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; BPB values are point estimates used for a data-pipeline diagnostic.
tables.data_and_statistics: Eight Gemma variants and one Pythia-410M reference are reported on Arxiv, Wiki and Stack; values use three decimal places. The group break separates Gemma from Pythia.
tables.evidence_relation: Diagnoses why Gemma is excluded from the Figure 4 perplexity analysis; it turns a potentially hidden missing subgroup into an explicit failure case.
design_strengths: Shows the raw abnormal values and a named reference.
Consistent three-decimal precision makes the anomaly visible.
Caption supplies document-length context and a plausible mechanism.
design_weaknesses: One Pythia reference cannot establish the anomaly's breadth.
No rolling-window configuration or exact sample count is in the table.
No uncertainty accompanies the exclusion diagnostic.
tables.reusable_pattern: When excluding a subgroup for a measurement failure, provide compact raw diagnostics, a reference, and the data-scale context in the appendix.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: The models used in Figure 7. The number of training tokens of these models is publicly available. We compute the number of pre-training FLOPs as 6 × #Parameters × #Tokens.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; parameters/tokens are inputs and FLOPs are a deterministic derived cost.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirty-eight public-token-count models are listed across five family groups. Parameter values use about two decimals, tokens one decimal, and FLOPs two decimals; the column precisions intentionally differ by quantity.
tables.evidence_relation: Provides the exact model/cost lookup for Figure 7 and documents the subset restriction created by public token counts.
design_strengths: Cost formula and units are visible in the caption/header.
The table makes every scatter point auditable.
Family ordering mirrors the model taxonomy.
design_weaknesses: Family groups rely mainly on row ordering and whitespace.
Training-token source URLs are not included.
Mixed precision across columns requires careful alignment.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair any compute scatter with a table of model, parameter, token and derived FLOPs values, plus a clear inclusion rule.

tables.reusable_pattern: Add a lower-cost preparation baseline as a column in an appendix table, keeping one row per task and the condition in the header.

caption.text: Table 6: The overall average Kendall’s τ across all benchmark pairs for models in each size bin.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; each row is an overall mean for a model-size stratum.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six size-bin rows plus All models report Direct evaluation and Train-before-test mean τ to two decimals; bins are [0,1), [1,2), [2,3), [6,7), [7,8), [9,10) B.

design_strengths: Simple three-column structure makes direction within each bin obvious.
All models row reconnects the stratified values to the headline.
Two-decimal precision is stable.
design_weaknesses: No number of models or benchmark pairs per bin is reported.
Bin boundary convention is not explained in the caption.
All models is separated mainly by position, not a strong rule.
tables.reusable_pattern: For size-stratified robustness, state bin boundaries, retain an overall row, and add n per bin so a large direction cannot hide a tiny stratum.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes local direct-versus-TBT rank disagreement; Figure 2 aggregates across 24 benchmarks; Figure 3 decomposes by category; Figures 4–5 test perplexity/downstream connections and base/IT boundaries; Figures 6–8 move to PCA, compute and family-controlled structure. Appendix Figures 9–10 and Tables 3–8 provide full matrices, a Gemma failure diagnostic, cost rows, few-shot and size/family stratifications; Figures 12–15 repeat the chain with ties-aware Kendall tau-b.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All objects use Figure N:/Table N: prefixes. Main result captions commonly state setup, comparison, aggregation and the directional finding; full matrices use shorter definition captions. Figure 1 uses bold Top/Bottom/Note subheads. Figure 7, Figure 11 and Tables 2, 5–7 are not self-contained because they omit subset, family, shot or denominator details.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–2 are taxonomy headers; Tables 3–7 use one-level headers with evaluation condition in the metric columns; Table 8 uses two grouped levels for Direct Evaluation/Train-before-test and PC1–PC5. Booktabs rules are consistent; row groups often rely on order/whitespace, and most result tables omit n and uncertainty.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Benchmark-specific fine-tuning, LoRA and validation selection are defined in the body/Appendix A.2; Figure 1 and Appendix C.1 expose the ranking-alignment interface; Figures 2–5 are headline/mechanism comparisons; Figures 6–8, Figure 11, Table 4 and Table 8 are PCA/compute structure; Tables 5–7 and Figures 12–15 are preparation, size/family and significance-aware robustness. No component-deletion ablation isolates LoRA, epochs, template or checkpoint selection.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figure 2's means are expanded by Figures 9–10; Figure 3's category result by Figure 13; Figure 4's Gemma exclusion by Table 3; Figure 7's compute subset by Table 4; Figure 6/8's PCA story by Figure 11 and Table 8. Appendix objects supply pairwise denominators, failure evidence, costs, stratification and alternate statistics rather than unrelated material.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern serif is stable in body, captions and tables, while DejaVu/Liberation/Arial sans-serif is used for plot labels; math symbols use the embedded Computer Modern fonts. Plot text is smaller than body text, and the dense matrices trade readability for complete coverage.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange is stable for direct/TBT bars; YlGnBu_r and 0–1 colorbars are stable for ordinary and tau-b matrices; one blue is reused for PCA bars; family colors recur in Figure 7 and Figure 11. Figure 1's 61-color husl cycle is an intentional identity encoding but has no legend and weak grayscale redundancy.

most_reusable_patterns: Matched direct/TBT panels retain the same task order, axis domain, colors and geometry, so differences read as evaluation-condition changes.
Aggregate per-task bars in the main text paired with complete benchmark-pair matrices in the appendix form a useful headline-to-audit ladder.
Rows-as-measurement-source and columns-as-task heatmaps expose perplexity/downstream links while retaining corpus heterogeneity.
Explained-variance bars followed by a compute scatter plus exact cost table and family/size tables progressively narrow a latent-structure interpretation.
The tau-b/ties robustness objects reuse the ordinary-tau geometry, changing the estimand without adding visual confounds.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: local rank-reversal demonstration and significance-aware TBT interface.
Figure 2 with Figures 9–10: aggregate 0.52→0.76 headline and complete pairwise audit.
Figures 4–6: perplexity mechanism, base/IT boundary, and score-matrix PC1 concentration.
Tables 3/4/7/8 with Figure 11 and Figures 12–15: failure, cost denominator, family boundary, full PC1 distribution and ties-aware closure.
failure_patterns: Figure 1 and the 24×24 matrices are information-dense at page scale; identity colors lack redundant shape/line encodings.
Most plots and Tables 5–8 are point estimates without seed aggregation, pair counts or per-task uncertainty; small size/family strata are therefore hard to calibrate.
Figure 7 has no trend/statistical summary and only includes models with public token counts, so PC1–compute is an observational subset relationship.
Figure 11 has no family legend; short captions for Table 2, Table 5–7 and Figure 7/11 omit key membership, condition or denominator information.
Gemma BPB exclusion, weak IT prediction (0.51) and Yi family TBT agreement (0.30) remain visible in appendix evidence but are not central to the headline mean.
The public source is partial: notebook/data support plot grammar and values, but no PDF TeX/table generator or exact final layout source is available.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses Figure 1's direct/TBT rank contrast to introduce equal preparation, Figures 2–5 to move from overall/category agreement to perplexity mechanism, Figures 6–8 to relate agreement to PCA/compute structure, and appendix matrices, diagnostics, stratified tables and tau-b robustness to close the pairwise and family-specific boundaries.
